name: Alert
summary: An inline message with a tone (info, success, warning, danger), placed next to the content it is about.
description: Use an alert for a message about one part of the page, such as a form or a card. For a message about the whole site use a banner, and for a short note that comes and goes use a toast.

classes.name: v-alert
classes.description: The alert box: an icon, then the body. Info tone by default.

classes.name: v-alert-body
classes.description: The text, which takes the remaining width.

classes.name: v-alert-title
classes.description: A bold lead-in at the start of the body.

classes.name: v-alert-danger
classes.description: Danger tone, for errors and failures.

states.description: Announced at once when it appears. Only for urgent messages added after the page loads.
Announced politely, for news that can wait.

a11y: The tone colour is backed by an icon and the words, so the meaning never rests on colour alone.
An alert that is in the page from the start needs no role; a live role only matters when it is added later.
Keep role="alert" for messages that must interrupt, such as a failed payment; overuse makes screen readers noisy.
Body text holds 4.5:1 contrast on every tone tint in both themes.
